turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Sir, before you see him, blood pressure is 128 over 82, pulse 76, temperature 36.7. He was shifting about in the chair outside, saying the back is paining.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, sister. Come in, please. Tell me what has been going on.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, my lower back is paining badly. It has been a few weeks, or actually since we shifted the house — I can't say which day it started, I'm sorry.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): No need to be sorry. When you shifted, was there a lot of lifting?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, boxes, and the fridge also, I carried most of it. I work in a godown, so lifting is my daily duty only. Doctor, is this a slip disc? I'm very worried.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will answer that once I have the full picture. Show me — is the pain only in the back, or does it travel down the leg?

[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): The pain itself is in the low back, both sides, more on the right. Sometimes it goes into the right buttock, not below the knee. Bending to pick something makes it worse.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any numbness or tingling in the legs, or around the private parts?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor, no numbness, and tingling also no. The leg just feels a bit tired after standing, that's all. Is tiredness a bad sign?
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tiredness alone is not a red flag. Any problem with the bladder or bowels — leaking, difficulty passing urine, or numbness when you pass stool?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Bladder is okay, I think. Last week, with the heat, I was drinking less water so I passed less urine, but no leaking, no burning, and bowels are normal only.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you lost any weight?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know. My trousers are a little loose, but during the move I was skipping lunch, running here and there. I never stood on a weighing scale.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): So are you actually losing weight, or is it just the missed meals?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I don't think I have lost weight. It is the meals only. Doctor, will I be able to continue my job? I can't sit at home.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or night sweats, or feeling ill in yourself?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Fever no. I checked at home, it was normal, and no sweats. But can this be an infection in the bone? My neighbour had TB of the spine and I keep thinking of that.

[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me say back what I have heard. Pain after lifting, no numbness, no bladder or bowel trouble, no fever, and you don't think you have lost weight — so spinal infection looks unlikely.

[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay, that is a relief, but the pain is still there. I am taking Dolo 650, one tablet by mouth, morning and night, and if the pain is more, one in the afternoon. Some days I forget the night tablet. Is three too much for the liver?
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Three tablets of 650 in a day is acceptable if there is no other paracetamol in the mix. Did you take anything else, from a chemist perhaps?

[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, the chemist gave a muscle relaxant, a small white tablet. I don't remember the name at all. I took it for two days and then I stopped, because I was feeling very drowsy in the godown. Is that dangerous, what I did?
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stopping it was sensible. What I was going to do is start diclofenac 50 mg twice a day, and send you for a lumbar spine X-ray today.

[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Diclofenac? Doctor, last time I took that my stomach was burning badly. Please don't give that. And the X-ray — is it really needed, what is the cost, I have duty tomorrow, I'm scared of all these tests.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then I will change the plan. No diclofenac, and we will not do the X-ray today.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Then what will you do? Is it something serious? Should I take leave? What if the pain shoots up in the night?

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): I examined you just now: the low back muscles are tight on the right, straight leg raise is free on both sides, and power in the legs is normal. My impression is mechanical low back pain from the lifting, not an emergency slip disc. Continue the Dolo, maximum three times a day, don't go above that. Use heat on the back, and no heavy lifting for now.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Only Dolo? It is not fully helping, doctor. Everyone is saying I must do an MRI. Will you send me for that?
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): We might do a scan if it does not settle. I am not ordering one today.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): If it does not settle — how many days is that? And if my leg suddenly goes numb, or I can't pass urine, do I wait? I'm really anxious, please tell me clearly.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's see you in two weeks. If there is new numbness, trouble controlling the urine, or the pain gets rapidly worse, come sooner, don't wait for that appointment.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Two weeks, alright. Can I do light work in the godown till then? And my wife says I should sleep on a hard bed — is that correct?
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Light duties, yes, but no lifting sacks. A hard bed is not required; a firm mattress is enough. Keep moving with short walks, and don't stay lying down all day.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, shall I book him into your afternoon clinic in two weeks?
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, please book a review in two weeks.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you. One last doubt — that white tablet which made me drowsy, shall I restart it at night only, half a tablet maybe?
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, leave that one completely. We don't know its name, and it made you drowsy at work. Paracetamol only, and we will review in two weeks.
